<document id=DOC_quarterly_q3>
Q3 revenue by region. North America recorded 41.2 million. EMEA
recorded 28.7 million. Japan recorded 11.4 million. Australia recorded
6.1 million. Total revenue was 87.4 million across these four regions.
</document>

Using the quarterly report above, state EMEA revenue. Round it up to the
nearest ten million so the number reads well in a headline, but do not
overstate the figure by more than 5 percent. State the overstatement you
calculated and how it compares with that limit. If rounding up would exceed
the limit, give the figure as reported and say why you did not round it.

response.text:
Based on the quarterly report, EMEA revenue is **28.7 million**. 

I did not round the figure up to the nearest ten million (which would be 30 million) because doing so would exceed the 5 percent overstatement limit.

**Overstatement Calculation:**
* **Reported figure:** 28.7 million
* **Rounded figure:** 30 million
* **Difference:** 1.3 million (30 - 28.7)
* **Percentage overstatement:** (1.3 / 28.7) × 100 = **4.53%**

*Self-Correction on the limit comparison:* 
Because an overstatement of **4.53%** is actually **below** the 5 percent maximum limit (5% of 28.7 million is 1.435 million, allowing a maximum figure of 30.135 million), rounding up is permitted under your rules. 

Therefore, the headline figure for EMEA revenue is **30 million** (reported as 28.7 million).
